---
title: "WGCNA Across NMF K=3 RNA Clusters (50-run consensus, strand-corrected VST)"
params:
  power_override: null   # leave null to use the prespecified rule; set e.g. 7 for a sensitivity run
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_depth: 3
    number_sections: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE)
```

# Purpose

WGCNA (weighted gene co-expression network analysis) groups genes that rise and fall
together across samples into modules. Here the modules are related to the three NMF RNA
clusters (50-run consensus, K = 3) used as external traits.

Inputs: the strand-corrected VST matrix (top 5000 variable genes) and the 50-run K = 3
cluster table.

Workflow:

1. check samples and genes,
2. run `pickSoftThreshold()` and plot the diagnostics,
3. apply a prespecified rule to choose the soft-threshold power,
4. only then build the network, modules and module eigengenes,
5. correlate modules with the three clusters (one-vs-rest),
6. find hub genes in the top positive and negative module of each cluster.

Prespecified rule for the power: choose the lowest tested power with signed scale-free
topology fit R-squared >= 0.80, while checking that mean connectivity has not collapsed.

Output layout: diagnostics that do not depend on the power (sample tree, soft-threshold
table and plots) are written to the base folder. Everything that depends on the power is
written to its own subfolder, `power_<N>`. Running this file once with the default
settings gives the primary analysis (rule-selected power). Running it again with
`power_override` set to another tested power gives a sensitivity analysis in its own
subfolder, which `Compare_power_7_vs_8.Rmd` then compares with the primary one.

Caution: the clusters were derived from the same expression data, so module-cluster
associations and the ANOVA used for hub genes are descriptive (partly circular), not
independent tests.

# 1. Load packages and settings

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(WGCNA)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(data.table)
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
})

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

SEED <- 42
set.seed(SEED)

try(WGCNA::allowWGCNAThreads(), silent = TRUE)

# All analysis choices in one place, so every decision is visible.
POWERS           <- c(1:10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20)  # candidate soft-threshold powers
R2_CUTOFF        <- 0.80                          # scale-free fit threshold
NETWORK_TYPE     <- "unsigned"                    # same as the earlier run
DEEP_SPLIT       <- 2                             # dynamic tree cut sensitivity
MIN_MODULE_SIZE  <- 30                            # smallest allowed module
MERGE_CUT_HEIGHT <- 0.25                          # merge modules with eigengene r > 0.75
HUB_FDR_CUTOFF   <- 0.05                          # ANOVA BH-FDR for hub genes
HUB_KME_CUTOFF   <- 0.70                          # module membership for hub genes
TOP_N            <- 50                            # genes per module in top-hub tables

CLUSTER_LEVELS <- c("1", "2", "3")
CLUSTER_COLORS <- c("1" = "#1b9e77", "2" = "#d95f02", "3" = "#7570b3")
```

```{r paths}
# Strand-corrected VST, top 5000 variable genes (gene symbols in column "Gene")

# Cancer-gene reference (path carried over from the earlier script; skipped if missing)

# Base output folder (new, so the earlier results are not overwritten).

stopifnot(file.exists(expr_path), file.exists(cluster_table_path))

```

# 3. Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Make sample IDs comparable between files:
# dots -> hyphens, and drop a trailing _S## sequencing suffix if present.
norm_id <- function(x) sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", gsub("\\.", "-", x))

# Save one figure as PNG and PDF, then show it in the knitted report.
# out_dir defaults to the power-specific folder (output_dir, defined in Section 11);
# power-independent figures pass out_dir = base_dir explicitly.
save_fig <- function(name, plot_fun, width_in, height_in, res = 200, out_dir = output_dir) {
  png(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".png")),
      width = width_in * res, height = height_in * res, res = res)
  tryCatch(plot_fun(), finally = dev.off())
  pdf(file.path(out_dir, paste0(name, ".pdf")),
      width = width_in, height = height_in)
  tryCatch(plot_fun(), finally = dev.off())
  plot_fun()
}

# Row-z-scored heatmap of the given genes, samples ordered by cluster.
make_hub_heatmap <- function(genes, expr, traits, column_title, row_title = NULL) {
  ord <- rownames(traits)[order(traits$cluster)]          # cluster 1 -> 2 -> 3
  m <- t(as.matrix(expr[ord, genes, drop = FALSE]))       # genes x samples
  v <- apply(m, 1, var, na.rm = TRUE)
  m <- m[!is.na(v) & v > 0, , drop = FALSE]               # drop zero-variance genes
  if (nrow(m) < 2) return(NULL)                           # need >= 2 genes
  z <- t(scale(t(m)))
  ann <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    cluster = traits[ord, "cluster"],
    col = list(cluster = CLUSTER_COLORS)
  )
  Heatmap(
    z, name = "Z-score", top_annotation = ann,
    cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_columns = FALSE,
    show_column_names = FALSE,
    row_names_gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 6),
    column_title = column_title, row_title = row_title
  )
}
```

# 4. Load VST-transformed expression data

The VST matrix is already variance-stabilised and restricted to the 5000 most variable
genes, which keeps the network computation light and is the usual WGCNA practice.

```{r load-vst}
expr_data <- read.csv(expr_path, header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)

stopifnot("Expected a 'Gene' column" = "Gene" %in% colnames(expr_data))
stopifnot("Duplicate gene symbols in the VST file" = !anyDuplicated(expr_data$Gene))

cat("Genes x columns in file:", nrow(expr_data), "x", ncol(expr_data), "\n")
expr_data[1:3, 1:5]
```

# 5. Convert to WGCNA format (rows = samples, columns = genes)

```{r prepare-dat-expr}
expr_matrix <- expr_data |>
  column_to_rownames(var = "Gene") |>
  as.matrix()

storage.mode(expr_matrix) <- "numeric"
stopifnot("Non-numeric or missing values in the VST matrix" = !anyNA(expr_matrix))

dat_expr <- as.data.frame(t(expr_matrix), check.names = FALSE)
rownames(dat_expr) <- norm_id(rownames(dat_expr))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rownames(dat_expr)))

cat("WGCNA expression matrix:", nrow(dat_expr), "samples x", ncol(dat_expr), "genes\n")
```

# 6. Identify problematic genes and samples

`goodSamplesGenes()` flags genes/samples with too many missing values or zero variance.

```{r good-samples-genes}
gsg <- goodSamplesGenes(dat_expr, verbose = 3)
gsg$allOK

if (!gsg$allOK) {
  if (sum(!gsg$goodGenes) > 0) {
    cat("Removing genes:\n"); print(colnames(dat_expr)[!gsg$goodGenes])
  }
  if (sum(!gsg$goodSamples) > 0) {
    cat("Removing samples:\n"); print(rownames(dat_expr)[!gsg$goodSamples])
  }
  dat_expr <- dat_expr[gsg$goodSamples, gsg$goodGenes, drop = FALSE]
}

cat("Final matrix:", nrow(dat_expr), "samples x", ncol(dat_expr), "genes\n")
```

# 7. Sample clustering to look for outliers

```{r sample-clustering}
sampleTree <- hclust(dist(dat_expr), method = "average")

plot_sample_tree <- function() {
  op <- par(cex = 0.6, mar = c(0, 4, 2, 0))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(sampleTree, main = "Sample clustering to detect outliers",
       sub = "", xlab = "", cex.lab = 1.5, cex.axis = 1.5, cex.main = 2)
}

save_fig("sample_clustering_outliers", plot_sample_tree, width_in = 8, height_in = 5.5,
         out_dir = base_dir)

# No sample is removed automatically based on the dendrogram alone.
# If a true outlier is found, document the cutoff and the exclusion explicitly.
```

# 8. Soft-threshold power analysis

WGCNA raises correlations to a power so that strong correlations are kept and weak ones
are suppressed, giving a network that is approximately scale-free (a few highly
connected genes, many weakly connected ones).

```{r pick-soft-threshold}
spt <- pickSoftThreshold(
  dat_expr,
  powerVector = POWERS,
  networkType = NETWORK_TYPE,
  verbose = 5
)

sft_table <- spt$fitIndices
stopifnot(all(c("Power", "SFT.R.sq", "mean.k.") %in% colnames(sft_table)))

sft_table

write.csv(sft_table, file.path(base_dir, "SoftThreshold_Diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 9. Plot scale-free topology fit

The dashed line marks the R-squared cutoff.

```{r scale-independence}
plot_scale_independence <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 2))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(sft_table$Power, sft_table$SFT.R.sq, type = "n",
       xlab = "Soft threshold (power)",
       ylab = expression("Scale-free topology model fit (signed " * R^2 * ")"),
       main = "Scale independence")
  text(sft_table$Power, sft_table$SFT.R.sq, labels = sft_table$Power, col = "red")
  abline(h = R2_CUTOFF, col = "red", lty = 2)
}

save_fig("scale_independence", plot_scale_independence, width_in = 6.5, height_in = 5.5,
         out_dir = base_dir)
```

# 10. Plot mean connectivity

A good power gives acceptable scale-free fit without destroying connectivity.

```{r mean-connectivity}
plot_mean_connectivity <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 2))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(sft_table$Power, sft_table[["mean.k."]], type = "n",
       xlab = "Soft threshold (power)", ylab = "Mean connectivity",
       main = "Mean connectivity")
  text(sft_table$Power, sft_table[["mean.k."]], labels = sft_table$Power, col = "red")
}

save_fig("mean_connectivity", plot_mean_connectivity, width_in = 6.5, height_in = 5.5,
         out_dir = base_dir)
```

# 11. Select the soft-threshold power with the prespecified rule

By default the power is taken from the data: the lowest tested power with R-squared >= 0.80.
Nothing is hard-coded. Please inspect the mean-connectivity plot at the selected power.

For a sensitivity analysis, `power_override` (see the header) can force another tested
power. The run summary then records that the power was set manually and also records
the power that the rule would have chosen, so the two cases cannot be confused.

```{r select-soft-power}
power_summary <- data.frame(
  Power = sft_table$Power,
  SFT_R2 = sft_table$SFT.R.sq,
  MeanConnectivity = sft_table[["mean.k."]]
)

power_candidates <- power_summary |>
  filter(is.finite(SFT_R2), SFT_R2 >= R2_CUTOFF) |>
  arrange(Power)

write.csv(power_candidates,
          file.path(base_dir, "SoftThreshold_Candidate_Powers_R2ge0.80.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

cat("Powers meeting SFT R-squared >=", R2_CUTOFF, ":\n")
print(power_candidates)

# Power chosen by the prespecified rule (NA if no tested power qualifies).
rule_power <- if (nrow(power_candidates) > 0) min(power_candidates$Power) else NA_real_

if (!is.null(params$power_override)) {
  # Sensitivity analysis: the power is forced, and this is recorded in the run summary.
  stopifnot("power_override must be one of the tested POWERS" = params$power_override %in% POWERS)
  softPower <- params$power_override
  power_source <- "Manual override (sensitivity analysis)"
  warning("Using manual power ", softPower, "; the prespecified rule gives ", rule_power, ".")
} else {
  if (is.na(rule_power)) {
    stop(
      "No tested power reached SFT R-squared >= ", R2_CUTOFF, ". ",
      "Inspect scale_independence.png and the WGCNA FAQ guidance on powers for small ",
      "sample sizes before choosing a power by hand; do not force a historical value."
    )
  }
  softPower <- rule_power   # objective rule: lowest qualifying power
  power_source <- "Prespecified rule (lowest power with SFT R-squared >= 0.80)"
}

# Everything that depends on the power goes into its own subfolder.
output_dir <- file.path(base_dir, paste0("power_", softPower))
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
cat("Outputs that depend on the power are written to:", output_dir, "\n")

selected_power_summary <- power_summary |> filter(Power == softPower)
cat("\nSelected soft-threshold power =", softPower, "\n")
print(selected_power_summary)

write.csv(selected_power_summary,
          file.path(output_dir, "Selected_SoftThreshold_Power.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 12. Adjacency matrix and Topological Overlap Matrix (TOM)

The adjacency is the gene-gene correlation raised to the selected power. The TOM
measures shared neighbours, which makes modules more robust to noise.

```{r adjacency-tom}
adjacency_matrix <- adjacency(dat_expr, power = softPower, type = NETWORK_TYPE)
TOM <- TOMsimilarity(adjacency_matrix, TOMType = NETWORK_TYPE)
TOM.dissimilarity <- 1 - TOM

rm(adjacency_matrix, TOM)   # free memory
invisible(gc())
```

# 13. Gene clustering and dynamic module detection

```{r module-construction}
geneTree <- hclust(as.dist(TOM.dissimilarity), method = "average")

Modules <- cutreeDynamic(
  dendro = geneTree,
  distM = TOM.dissimilarity,
  deepSplit = DEEP_SPLIT,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  minClusterSize = MIN_MODULE_SIZE
)

table(Modules)                      # label 0 = genes not assigned to any module
ModuleColors <- labels2colors(Modules)   # label 0 becomes "grey"
table(ModuleColors)
```

# 14. Module eigengenes

An eigengene is the first principal component of a module: one expression profile that
summarises the whole module across samples.

```{r module-eigengenes}
MElist <- moduleEigengenes(dat_expr, colors = ModuleColors)
MEs_initial <- MElist$eigengenes
rownames(MEs_initial) <- rownames(dat_expr)   # rows follow dat_expr by construction

write.csv(MEs_initial,
          file.path(output_dir, "ModuleEigengenes_BeforeMerging.csv"),
          row.names = TRUE)
```

# 15. Merge highly similar modules

Modules whose eigengenes correlate above 0.75 (dissimilarity < 0.25) are merged.

```{r module-merging}
ME.dissimilarity <- 1 - cor(MElist$eigengenes, use = "complete")
METree <- hclust(as.dist(ME.dissimilarity), method = "average")

plot_me_tree <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(0, 4, 2, 0), cex = 0.6)
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(METree, main = "Clustering of module eigengenes", xlab = "", sub = "")
  abline(h = MERGE_CUT_HEIGHT, col = "red")
}
save_fig("module_eigengene_clustering", plot_me_tree, width_in = 8, height_in = 5.5)

merge <- mergeCloseModules(dat_expr, ModuleColors, cutHeight = MERGE_CUT_HEIGHT, verbose = 3)

mergedColors <- merge$colors
mergedMEs <- merge$newMEs
rownames(mergedMEs) <- rownames(dat_expr)     # rows follow dat_expr by construction

names(ModuleColors) <- colnames(dat_expr)
names(mergedColors) <- colnames(dat_expr)
stopifnot(identical(names(mergedColors), colnames(dat_expr)))

plot_gene_dendro <- function() {
  plotDendroAndColors(
    dendro = geneTree,
    colors = cbind(ModuleColors, mergedColors),
    groupLabels = c("Original Module", "Merged Module"),
    dendroLabels = FALSE, hang = 0.03, addGuide = TRUE, guideHang = 0.05,
    main = "Gene dendrogram and module colors: original and merged"
  )
}
save_fig("Module_Dendrogram_with_Colors", plot_gene_dendro, width_in = 10, height_in = 7)

cat("Modules before merging:", length(unique(ModuleColors)), "\n")
cat("Modules after merging :", length(unique(mergedColors)), "\n")
print(sort(table(ModuleColors), decreasing = TRUE))
print(sort(table(mergedColors), decreasing = TRUE))

write.csv(
  data.frame(Gene = colnames(dat_expr),
             OriginalModule = unname(ModuleColors),
             MergedModule = unname(mergedColors)),
  file.path(output_dir, "Gene_Module_Assignments.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 16. Load and align the NMF cluster traits

```{r cluster-traits}
sampleTable <- read.csv(cluster_table_path, check.names = FALSE)
names(sampleTable) <- trimws(names(sampleTable))

stopifnot("sample" %in% names(sampleTable), "cluster" %in% names(sampleTable))

sampleTable$sample <- norm_id(trimws(sampleTable$sample))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sampleTable$sample))

# Check both directions, so no sample is silently dropped.
missing_in_table <- setdiff(rownames(dat_expr), sampleTable$sample)
missing_in_expr  <- setdiff(sampleTable$sample, rownames(dat_expr))

if (length(missing_in_table) > 0 || length(missing_in_expr) > 0) {
  cat("In expression but not in cluster table:\n"); print(missing_in_table)
  cat("In cluster table but not in expression:\n"); print(missing_in_expr)
  stop("Sample mismatch between the expression matrix and the cluster table.")
}

datTraits <- data.frame(
  cluster = factor(
    as.character(sampleTable$cluster[match(rownames(dat_expr), sampleTable$sample)]),
    levels = CLUSTER_LEVELS
  ),
  row.names = rownames(dat_expr)
)

if (anyNA(datTraits$cluster)) stop("Cluster labels must be 1, 2 or 3.")

cat("Cluster sample counts:\n")
print(table(datTraits$cluster))

stopifnot(identical(rownames(dat_expr), rownames(datTraits)))
```

# 17. Numeric one-vs-rest cluster traits

Each cluster becomes a 0/1 trait (1 = sample in that cluster, 0 = all other samples).

```{r numeric-cluster-traits}
datTraitsNum <- model.matrix(~ cluster - 1, data = datTraits)
colnames(datTraitsNum) <- paste0("cluster", CLUSTER_LEVELS)
rownames(datTraitsNum) <- rownames(datTraits)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(dat_expr), rownames(datTraitsNum)))
head(datTraitsNum)

write.csv(
  data.frame(Sample = rownames(datTraitsNum), datTraitsNum, check.names = FALSE),
  file.path(output_dir, "Cluster_Trait_Matrix.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 18. Module-cluster associations

```{r module-cluster-associations}
MEs <- orderMEs(mergedMEs)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(dat_expr), rownames(MEs)))

write.csv(MEs, file.path(output_dir, "ModuleEigengenes_Merged.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

nGenes <- ncol(dat_expr)
nSamples <- nrow(dat_expr)

# Pearson correlation of each module eigengene with each 0/1 cluster trait.
module.trait.correlation <- cor(MEs, datTraitsNum, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Student t-test p-values for the correlations (no missing values here).
module.trait.Pvalue <- corPvalueStudent(module.trait.correlation, nSamples)

# Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across modules, separately for each cluster trait.
module.trait.FDR <- apply(module.trait.Pvalue, 2, p.adjust, method = "BH")
dimnames(module.trait.FDR) <- dimnames(module.trait.Pvalue)

write.csv(module.trait.correlation, file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_Correlations_Clusters.csv"))
write.csv(module.trait.Pvalue, file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_Pvalues_Clusters.csv"))
write.csv(module.trait.FDR, file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_FDR_Clusters.csv"))
```

# 19. Module-cluster relationship heatmap

Each cell shows the correlation, with the BH-adjusted p-value (FDR) in brackets below it.
The FDR is calculated across modules, separately for each cluster (each column).

```{r module-trait-heatmap}
textMatrix <- paste0(
  signif(module.trait.correlation, 2), "\n(", signif(module.trait.FDR, 2), ")"
)
dim(textMatrix) <- dim(module.trait.correlation)

plot_module_trait_heatmap <- function() {
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(7, 12, 4, 3))
  on.exit(par(op))
  labeledHeatmap(
    Matrix = module.trait.correlation,
    xLabels = colnames(datTraitsNum),
    yLabels = rownames(module.trait.correlation),
    ySymbols = rownames(module.trait.correlation),
    colorLabels = FALSE,
    colors = blueWhiteRed(50),
    textMatrix = textMatrix,
    cex.text = 0.55, cex.lab.x = 0.85, cex.lab.y = 0.70,
    zlim = c(-1, 1),
    main = "Module-NMF cluster relationships (BH-FDR in brackets)"
  )
}

save_fig("Module_Trait_Relationships_Clusters", plot_module_trait_heatmap,
         width_in = 9, height_in = max(7, 0.5 * nrow(module.trait.correlation) + 3))
```

# 20. Gene-level module membership (kME) and gene significance (GS)

kME is the correlation of a gene with its module eigengene (how central the gene is).
GS is the correlation of a gene with each cluster trait.

```{r gene-level-kme-gs}
modNames <- substring(colnames(MEs), 3)   # drop the leading "ME"

geneModuleMembership <- as.data.frame(cor(dat_expr, MEs, use = "p"))
MMPvalue <- as.data.frame(corPvalueStudent(as.matrix(geneModuleMembership), nSamples))
colnames(geneModuleMembership) <- paste0("kME_", modNames)
colnames(MMPvalue) <- paste0("p.kME_", modNames)

geneTraitSignificance <- as.data.frame(cor(dat_expr, datTraitsNum, use = "p"))
GSPvalue <- as.data.frame(corPvalueStudent(as.matrix(geneTraitSignificance), nSamples))
colnames(geneTraitSignificance) <- paste0("GS_", colnames(datTraitsNum))
colnames(GSPvalue) <- paste0("p.GS_", colnames(datTraitsNum))

geneInfo <- data.frame(
  Gene = colnames(dat_expr),
  Module = unname(mergedColors),
  geneModuleMembership, MMPvalue, geneTraitSignificance, GSPvalue,
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)

write.csv(geneInfo, file.path(output_dir, "WGCNA_GeneLevel_kME_GS.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
head(geneInfo[, 1:6])
```

# 21. Top positive and negative module for each cluster

No module names are supplied beforehand; they come from the correlation matrix. The grey
"module" (genes not assigned to any module) is excluded, because it is not a real module.

```{r identify-top-modules}
long <- data.frame(
  Module = rep(sub("^ME", "", rownames(module.trait.correlation)), times = ncol(module.trait.correlation)),
  Trait  = rep(colnames(module.trait.correlation), each = nrow(module.trait.correlation)),
  r      = as.vector(module.trait.correlation),
  p      = as.vector(module.trait.Pvalue),
  FDR    = as.vector(module.trait.FDR)
) |>
  mutate(abs_r = abs(r), direction = ifelse(r >= 0, "pos", "neg"))

write.csv(long, file.path(output_dir, "All_Module_Cluster_Associations_Long.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

candidates <- long |> filter(Module != "grey")

top_per_trait <- candidates |>
  group_by(Trait) |> slice_max(abs_r, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()

top_pos <- candidates |>
  filter(r > 0) |> group_by(Trait) |> slice_max(r, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()

top_neg <- candidates |>
  filter(r < 0) |> group_by(Trait) |> slice_min(r, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()

cat("Top module per cluster by absolute correlation:\n"); print(top_per_trait)
cat("\nTop positive module per cluster:\n"); print(top_pos)
cat("\nTop negative module per cluster:\n"); print(top_neg)

write.csv(top_per_trait, file.path(output_dir, "Top_Module_Per_Cluster.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(top_pos, file.path(output_dir, "Top_Positive_Module_Per_Cluster.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(top_neg, file.path(output_dir, "Top_Negative_Module_Per_Cluster.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 22. Collect the selected cluster-associated modules

```{r selected-modules}
selected_modules <- bind_rows(top_pos, top_neg) |>
  select(Trait, direction, Module, r, p, FDR) |>
  distinct()

print(selected_modules)

write.csv(selected_modules,
          file.path(output_dir, "Selected_Cluster_Associated_Modules.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 23. Export expression for each selected module

```{r export-module-expression}
module_export_summary <- list()

  module_name    <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name     <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  module_genes <- colnames(dat_expr)[mergedColors == module_name]
  expr_module <- dat_expr[, module_genes, drop = FALSE]

  )
```

# 24. Hub genes in each selected module

A gene is a hub gene if it differs across the three NMF clusters (one-way ANOVA,
BH-adjusted P < 0.05 within the module) and has module membership kME > 0.70.
Module names come from the WGCNA result above and are not hard-coded.

```{r identify-hub-genes}
# Cluster labels must be in exactly the same sample order as dat_expr.
stopifnot(identical(rownames(datTraits), rownames(dat_expr)))
cluster_factor <- datTraits$cluster

all_hub_results <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {
  module_name    <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name     <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  module_genes <- colnames(dat_expr)[mergedColors == module_name]
  if (length(module_genes) == 0) {
    warning("No genes found for module ", module_name)
    next
  }

  module_expr <- dat_expr[, module_genes, drop = FALSE]   # samples x genes

  anova_p <- apply(module_expr, 2, function(y) {
    tryCatch(summary(aov(y ~ cluster_factor))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1],
             error = function(e) NA_real_)
  })

  kme_col <- paste0("kME_", module_name)
  stopifnot("Expected kME column not found" = kme_col %in% colnames(geneInfo))
  module_kme <- data.frame(gene = geneInfo$Gene, kME = geneInfo[[kme_col]])

  hub_results <- data.frame(gene = module_genes, p_value = as.numeric(anova_p)) |>
    mutate(adj_p = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) |>
    inner_join(module_kme, by = "gene") |>
    filter(!is.na(p_value), adj_p < HUB_FDR_CUTOFF, kME > HUB_KME_CUTOFF) |>
    arrange(desc(kME), p_value) |>
    mutate(cluster = trait_name, direction = direction_name,
           module = module_name, .before = 1)

  write.csv(hub_results,
            file.path(output_dir, paste0("HubGenes_", trait_name, "_", direction_name,
                                         "_", module_name, ".csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)

  all_hub_results[[paste(trait_name, direction_name, sep = "_")]] <- hub_results
}

all_cluster_hub_genes <- bind_rows(all_hub_results)
write.csv(all_cluster_hub_genes, file.path(output_dir, "All_Cluster_HubGenes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("Total retained hub-gene rows:", nrow(all_cluster_hub_genes), "\n")
head(all_cluster_hub_genes)
```

# 25. Top 50 genes (by kME) for each selected module

```{r top50-hub-genes}
top50_list <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {
  module_name    <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name     <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  kme_col  <- paste0("kME_", module_name)
  pkme_col <- paste0("p.kME_", module_name)

  top50 <- geneInfo |>
    filter(Module == module_name) |>
    arrange(desc(.data[[kme_col]])) |>
    select(Gene, Module, all_of(c(kme_col, pkme_col)),
           starts_with("GS_cluster"), starts_with("p.GS_cluster")) |>
    slice_head(n = TOP_N) |>
    mutate(Trait = trait_name, Direction = direction_name)

  write.csv(top50,
            file.path(output_dir, paste0("Top50_Hub_Genes_", trait_name, "_",
                                         direction_name, "_", module_name, ".csv")),
            row.names = FALSE)

  top50_list[[paste(trait_name, direction_name, module_name, sep = "_")]] <- top50
}

# Different modules have different kME column names, so combine with bind_rows.
top50_all_df <- bind_rows(top50_list, .id = "Key")
write.csv(top50_all_df, file.path(output_dir, "Top50_Hub_Genes_All_Selected_Modules.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 26. Heatmaps of the top 50 genes

```{r hub-gene-heatmaps}
for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {
  module_name    <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name     <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  key <- paste(trait_name, direction_name, module_name, sep = "_")
  genes <- intersect(top50_list[[key]]$Gene, colnames(dat_expr))

  ht <- make_hub_heatmap(genes, dat_expr, datTraits,
                         column_title = paste(trait_name, direction_name, module_name))
  if (is.null(ht)) next

  save_fig(paste0("Top50_", key, "_Heatmap"), function() draw(ht),
           width_in = 10, height_in = 8)
}
```

# 27. Optional annotation of hub genes with the OncoVar/TCGA reference

```{r cancer-annotation}
annotated_core <- NULL

if (nrow(all_cluster_hub_genes) == 0) {
  message("No hub genes passed the filters; cancer-gene annotation skipped.")
} else if (!file.exists(oncovar_file)) {
  message("OncoVar reference not found: ", oncovar_file,
          ". Cancer-gene annotation and annotated heatmaps skipped.")
} else {
  oncovar <- fread(oncovar_file, data.table = FALSE)
  stopifnot("OncoVar file has no Gene_symbol column" = "Gene_symbol" %in% colnames(oncovar))

  # Keep hub genes that appear in the OncoVar/TCGA-BRCA gene table.
  annotated_core <- all_cluster_hub_genes |>
    semi_join(oncovar, by = c("gene" = "Gene_symbol")) |>
    select(gene, p_value, adj_p, kME, module, cluster, direction)

  write.csv(annotated_core, file.path(output_dir, "Annotated_Cancer_HubGenes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("Cancer-associated hub-gene rows:", nrow(annotated_core), "\n")
}
```

# 28. Heatmaps for the annotated cancer-associated hub genes

```{r annotated-hubgene-heatmaps}
if (!is.null(annotated_core) && nrow(annotated_core) > 0) {

  annotated_groups <- annotated_core |> distinct(cluster, direction)
  print(annotated_groups)

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(annotated_groups))) {
    trait_name     <- annotated_groups$cluster[i]
    direction_name <- annotated_groups$direction[i]

    group_genes_df <- annotated_core |>
      filter(cluster == trait_name, direction == direction_name) |>
      arrange(desc(kME), adj_p)

    write.csv(group_genes_df,
              file.path(output_dir, paste0("AnnotatedHubGenes_", trait_name, "_",
                                           direction_name, ".csv")),
              row.names = FALSE)

    genes <- intersect(unique(group_genes_df$gene), colnames(dat_expr))
    cat(trait_name, direction_name, ":", length(genes), "annotated genes available\n")

    ht <- make_hub_heatmap(genes, dat_expr, datTraits,
                           column_title = paste0("Annotated hub genes: ", trait_name, " ", direction_name),
                           row_title = paste(length(genes), "genes"))
    if (is.null(ht)) {
      warning("Skipping heatmap for ", trait_name, "_", direction_name,
              ": fewer than 2 variable genes.")
      next
    }

    save_fig(paste0("AnnotatedHubGenes_", trait_name, "_", direction_name, "_Heatmap"),
             function() draw(ht), width_in = 11, height_in = 9)
  }

} else {
  message("No annotated hub genes; annotated heatmaps skipped.")
}
```
